slot.brief: Two satellites orbiting the same (or related) central bodies; use T² ∝ r³ to compare orbital periods or radii, with simple numeric scaling.

stem: Two satellites orbit the same planet in circular orbits of radii $r$ and $4r$. If the satellite at radius $r$ has an orbital period of $6$ h, what is the period of the other satellite?

verdicts.working: For circular orbits around the same planet, T is proportional to r^(3/2). Thus T2 = 6 × 4^(3/2) = 48 h.

working:
$T^2\propto r^3$; $\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}=\left(\dfrac{4r}{r}\right)^{3/2}=8$; $T_2=8(6)=48$ h.

Independent check: For circular orbits around the same planet, T is proportional to r^(3/2). Thus T2 = 6 × 4^(3/2) = 48 h.
solution:
For satellites orbiting the same planet, Kepler’s third law gives $T\propto r^{3/2}$.
$$\frac{T_2}{T_1}=\left(\frac{4r}{r}\right)^{3/2}=8$$
Thus, $T_2=8(6)=48\text{ h}$.
